items.title: Airline-agent past interaction: booking and baggage correction
items.body: In a past airline-agent interaction (policy stated current time 2024-05-15), user sought to remove a passenger, then cancel reservation H9ZU1C. Assistant correctly stated passenger count cannot be changed; after obtaining user ID/reason and looking up reservation, assistant declined cancellation because user said “another reason,” booking was economy, no insurance, and not within 24 hours. User then requested cheapest direct round trip from either EWR/JFK to West Coast, May 20–25. Searches found JFK–SEA round trip, flights HAT069 ($51) and HAT276 ($55), basic economy, $106; assistant requested confirmation/insurance choice, then booked after explicit yes, no insurance, and payment instruction to use $39 gift card then $67 from $203 gift card. Booking tool returned HATHAT; final booking included one checked bag, consistent with policy’s silver + basic economy allowance (one per passenger). Important observed misstep: before booking assistant claimed silver basic economy allowance was two free checked bags, then corrected itself after user challenged; policy specifies silver = 1 free bag per basic-economy passenger. Also, user said “all” of allowance and tool input used total_baggages:1; one traveler. Searches appear not exhaustive across all West Coast destinations (only SFO, LAX, SEA, PHX, LAS), so “lowest-priced” claim was limited by queried destinations, not proven globally. Record does not establish additional grading outcomes.

items.title: Airline support episode: passenger, cancellation, baggage, search
items.body:
Observed in a supplied airline-agent transcript/policy (scope: this episode; no grading details provided): reservation H9ZU1C had three passengers including Ethan; the policy says passenger edits cannot change passenger count, so refusing to remove one passenger was consistent. User supplied ID mia_kim_4397 and cancellation reason 'another reason'; reservation was created 2024-05-01, economy, no insurance, and interaction time was 2024-05-15. Under the supplied cancellation rules, none of the listed eligibility criteria appeared met, so not cancelling was consistent based on available data.
For a later booking, profile showed silver membership and one passenger in basic economy. Policy baggage table gives silver basic-economy 1 free bag per passenger. Assistant initially claimed two free bags, then corrected itself; reservation tool result recorded total_baggages=1 and nonfree_baggages=0. The final correction was consistent with policy, initial statement was not.
Flight search returned JFK–SEA HAT069 at basic economy $51 for May 20 and SEA–JFK HAT276 at $55 for May 25; the assistant reported $106 total and booked after explicit confirmation, no insurance, one free bag, using $39 and $67 from profile gift cards. Search covered listed West Coast airports encountered (SFO, LAX, SEA, PHX, LAS) but one combined tool call contained multiple simultaneous search calls, contrary to supplied instruction to make only one tool call at a time. The transcript does not establish whether every possible relevant airport/destination was exhaustively considered, so the 'lowest-priced' assertion is only supported by searched results. Reservation ID returned as HATHAT.

items.title: Airline booking experience: tool discipline and baggage allowance
items.body: In a past airline-agent interaction (policy context supplied in that task), passenger count could not be changed, and cancellation was allowed only if one of the stated criteria applied; a booking about 15 days away, economy, uninsured, and cancelled for a personal/other reason did not qualify. For booking searches, compare complete outbound/return combinations and cabin-specific fares across the requested airports/destinations before claiming the cheapest. Caution: the policy required only one tool call per turn, but the prior assistant issued batches of simultaneous search calls, so do not repeat that pattern where the same constraint applies. The prior assistant also incorrectly said silver basic-economy passengers had two free checked bags, then corrected itself: the supplied policy specifies one free checked bag per silver basic-economy passenger; the final one-passenger booking included one. Follow the exact allowance table and avoid adding bags beyond the user's need. Past booking used a $39 gift card plus $67 from a second card toward $106; profile payment details can differ from old reservation payment records, so verify current profile methods rather than assume.

items.title: Airline booking workflow lessons from prior public experience
items.body: In a prior airline-agent interaction under a policy requiring confirmation before booking/modification/cancellation, the agent correctly obtained user ID, searched direct flights across EWR/JFK and several West Coast destinations, compared available outbound/return options by basic-economy prices, presented a $106 JFK–SEA round trip, and got explicit confirmation before booking. Reservation tool output confirmed the itinerary, split gift-card charges ($39 + $67), no insurance, and one bag. It later corrected an earlier mistaken claim that silver members get two free checked bags in basic economy: supplied policy actually gives silver 1 bag per basic-economy passenger (thus 1 for this single passenger). For future work, calculate baggage strictly from membership tier, cabin, and passenger count before stating it; reconcile spoken allowance, requested bag count, and booking arguments/output. Do not assume prior actions were error-free: airport/destination search covered listed West Coast candidates, but exhaustive scope was not established. Cancellation example: passenger count cannot be changed; user pivoted to cancellation, provided ID/reason, reservation details showed booking May 1 versus current May 15, economy and no insurance, so the stated cancellation eligibility criteria were not met; avoid calling cancellation API absent eligibility. No separate evaluation feedback beyond level none.

items.title: Airline booking experience: baggage allowance and search scope
items.body: In a past airline-agent interaction, the policy specified silver membership entitles each basic-economy passenger to 1 free checked bag (2 in economy, 3 in business). The assistant initially incorrectly told a one-passenger silver/basic-economy customer they had two free checked bags, then corrected itself; the booking had 1 bag and this matched policy. Lesson/caution: calculate baggage allowance from the exact membership, cabin, and passenger count before stating it or submitting booking fields; do not confuse allowances across cabins. In the same interaction, cheapest direct round trip was reported based on searches across the available listed West Coast destinations (SFO, LAX, SEA, PHX, LAS) and both New York airports, but search results are only as comprehensive as the destinations/origin-return combinations actually queried; avoid claiming a global cheapest fare beyond the searched scope. No separate evaluation feedback was provided.

items.title: Airline-agent past interaction observations
items.body: In a prior airline-agent interaction (policy context current 2024-05-15), the assistant first said Ethan could not be removed because passenger count cannot change; user then requested cancellation of H9ZU1C, supplied user ID mia_kim_4397 and reason “another reason.” Reservation lookup showed created May 1, economy, no insurance, so cancellation was not eligible under the listed criteria; assistant declined. For a later request for cheapest direct NYC–West Coast round trip May 20–25, assistant searched routes and found JFK–SEA HAT069 ($51 basic economy) and SEA–JFK HAT276 ($55), total $106; user confirmed booking with no insurance and free baggage, and requested $39 gift card then the larger card. Booking succeeded as HATHAT, charging $39 and $67, with 1 bag. Important applicable policy facts: silver member basic-economy allowance is 1 free checked bag per passenger; assistant initially incorrectly said 2, then corrected this after user challenged it. Preserve uncertainty: this is a single transcript, and no evaluation feedback beyond level “none” was supplied; do not infer a grading outcome.

items.title: Airline booking and reservation policy lessons
items.body: From a prior airline-agent interaction (policy-specific; verify current policy/tools before applying): For booking, get user ID, establish itinerary/trip type, search all applicable origin/destination options and dates before claiming the cheapest, then identify cabin/availability/prices. Obtain passenger details from user/profile as permitted, ask about insurance, calculate baggage allowance from membership + cabin + passenger count, and confirm complete action details before booking. In one case, silver + basic economy allowed 1 free checked bag per passenger (not 2); the booking result confirmed 1 bag. Check arithmetic and selected payment methods/balances; prior $106 fare was split $39 + $67 across profile gift cards and tool confirmed booking. For cancellation, obtain user ID, reservation ID, and reason; inspect reservation and verify eligibility before cancellation tool call (e.g. within 24 hours, airline cancellation, business cabin, or qualifying insurance/reason; check flown segments and transfer if policy requires). A reservation made May 1, evaluated May 15, economy without insurance, for 'other' reason did not meet stated criteria. For passenger changes, policy disallows changing passenger count, including via human agent; explain this clearly. Past tool results / date availability and reservation ID formatting can be surprising, so report only confirmed results and stop to ask/clarify if essential facts are missing.
